artifacts.notes: The content-delivery route https://www.vatican.va/content/dam/wss/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_decree_19641121_orientalium-ecclesiarum_lt.html returned a byte-identical 51347-byte response with this SHA-256 on 2026-07-24; the alias is not duplicated, while the corresponding press route returned HTTP 404. The response contains articles 1-30, formula and date, a vacatio-legis notice, and a 43-entry subscription block that is abridged relative to the Acta. It then appends the distinct Lumen gentium Notificationes, embedded 6 March 1964 Doctrinal Commission declaration, and Nota explicativa praevia before presenting the Decree's notes; those works are not part of Orientalium Ecclesiarum. The HTML title and keywords misspell the incipit as Orientalium ecclesiarium. The web note for Basil gives PG 32, 669 B where the Acta prints 689 B, and the web formula differs slightly from the Acta formula. Exact bytes are identified but not retained.
artifacts.rights_basis: The Vatican portal Legal Notes, reviewed 2026-07-24 at https://www.vatican.va/content/vatican/en/legal-notes.html, limit portal content to personal and non-profit viewing and prohibit collection, reproduction, dissemination, or transfer without prior written authorization from the Dicastery for Communication. No repository redistribution permission was established.

edition.notes: A dated Vatican delivery state of the Latin Decree. The exact response contains articles 1-30, formula and date, a vacatio notice, an abridged subscription block, consolidated notes, and unrelated Lumen gentium apparatus appended by the delivery page. Those distinct works are not absorbed into this edition.

alternate_titles: Decree on the Catholic Churches of the Eastern Rite
work.author: Second Vatican Council
work.description: The Second Vatican Council's Decree on the Catholic Eastern Churches, solemnly promulgated by Pope Paul VI on 21 November 1964. Its numbered articles 1-30 address the Churches' dignity, patrimony, governance, sacramental discipline, worship, and relations with separated Eastern Churches.
